svg.title: OPAL user personas
svg.desc: Three personas: the planner, the field operator and the data modeller, with goals, frustrations and needs.
svg.text: ARTIFACT — USER PERSONAS
Three roles, one spreadsheet between them
Each role touched the same data at a different stage, in a very different place.
PL
The planner
DATA SERVICES · OFFICE
Turns the Data Modelling team's standard (data types,
durations, repetitions) into a data-collection plan for each
customer project.
Desktop
Plans ahead of the site visit
Owns the plan
GOALS
A plan that matches the modelling standard, first time
Reuse the core material set, then add the extras each
project needs
FRUSTRATIONS WITH THE SPREADSHEET
A new spreadsheet for every project
Formulas break whenever the plan changes
No view of what was actually collected until post-
processing
WHAT OPAL HAS TO GIVE THEM
A shared catalogue, planned runs generated from the
standard, and live progress from the site.
OP
The field operator
DATA SERVICES · CUSTOMER SITE
Travels to the customer's production floor and runs the
machine through every planned run, recording each scan.
Gloves and mask
Bright production floor
Limited to no internet
GOALS
Finish all planned runs in as few days on site as
possible
Record every scan correctly the first time
The option to work from a tablet, not only a laptop
FRUSTRATIONS WITH THE SPREADSHEET
Typing scan IDs and times by hand into a spreadsheet
Missed or skipped measurements mean editing formulas mid-
run
End-of-day checks mean reading raw spreadsheet rows
WHAT OPAL HAS TO GIVE THEM
Glove-sized controls on a tablet, work that saves without a
connection, a clear way to retry a run, and an end-of-day
view of what was collected.
DM
The data modeller
DATA MODELLING · OFFICE
Sets the data standard for each project, then uses the
collected and annotated scans to train detection models per
material.
Desktop
Downstream of every other step
Owns the standard
GOALS
Enough correctly tagged data of each type to train
reliable models
Data that can be trusted without re-checking by hand
FRUSTRATIONS WITH THE SPREADSHEET
Data arrives only after two rounds of scripts
Errors found late are usually unrecoverable
A wrong material tag corrupts the model, not just a row
WHAT OPAL HAS TO GIVE THEM
Every scan traceable to its planned run and material, with
reviewed annotations, on an internal platform.
